title: Labor-Only Claim Settlement Worksheet: Harbison 5-Year and 10-Year Labor Protection
content:
This worksheet defines the approved amount of a claim filed against a Harbison 5-Year Labor Protection or Harbison 10-Year Labor Protection contract, the labor-only tiers of Harbison Protection Contracts.

**The claim and its records.** The claim settled is the claim filed on the contract on the date of handling. Its service call, failed unit, failed component and failure date are the ones recorded on that claim; the failure date is the completed date of that service call.

**Defined quantities.**

1. *Labor net* — the repair labor line charged on the claim's service call under the price-book task of the failed component, less the Comfort Club member repair discount posted against that labor line.
2. *Component sublimit* — the tier's motor labor sublimit for a blower, inducer or condenser fan motor; its control labor sublimit for a control board, defrost board or gas valve; its compressor, coil or heat exchanger labor sublimit for those components. There is no sublimit for any other covered component, and the labor net of such a component is then not capped.
3. *Labor allowed* — the labor net up to the component sublimit, that is, the lesser of the two.
4. *Labor payable* — equal to the labor allowed.
5. *Lead claim* — the claim on the service call whose failed component carries the largest repair labor line charged on that call.
6. *Diagnostic net* — the diagnostic fee charged on the claim's service call less the member diagnostic rate posted against it.
7. *Premium net* — the after-hours premium charged on that call less the member premium discount posted against it.
8. *Diagnostic payable* — the diagnostic net multiplied by the tier's own diagnostic coverage, which is one where the tier covers the diagnostic fee and zero where it does not; payable only on the lead claim, and zero on any other claim of the call.
9. *Premium payable* — the premium net multiplied by the tier's own after-hours coverage, one where the tier covers the after-hours premium and zero where it does not; payable only on the lead claim, and zero on any other claim of the call.
10. Parts are never paid on a labor-only tier.

**The approved amount.** The labor-only claim payable is the labor payable plus the diagnostic payable plus the premium payable, capped at the tier's per-claim limit and at the contract's remaining claim benefit — the least of those three figures. The approved amount written on the decision is that capped figure rounded to the cent, half up, with every intermediate figure kept unrounded.

The tier figures read here — the labor sublimits, the per-claim limit, and whether the tier covers the diagnostic fee and the after-hours premium — are the ones listed for the tier in the Harbison Protection Contracts schedules.

**Worked figure (hypothetical inputs; the sublimit and limit figures below are illustrative and are not schedule values).**

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| failed component | blower motor, the only claim on the call |
| repair labor line | $640.00 |
| member repair discount on that line | $64.00 |
| illustrative motor sublimit | $500.00 |
| diagnostic fee, member diagnostic rate | $129.00, $29.00 |
| tier covers the diagnostic fee | no |
| after-hours premium on the call | none |
| illustrative per-claim limit | $2000.00 |
| remaining claim benefit | $4200.00 |

- Labor net: $640.00 less $64.00 is $576.00. Labor allowed: the lesser of $576.00 and $500.00 is $500.00, and the labor payable is $500.00.
- The claim is the lead claim. Diagnostic net $100.00, multiplied by a diagnostic coverage of zero, gives $0.00. Premium payable $0.00.
- Claim payable $500.00; the caps of $2000.00 and $4200.00 do not bind. Approved amount: **$500.00**.

Same inputs with $420.35 of claim benefit remaining: the least of $500.00, $2000.00 and $420.35 is $420.35, and the approved amount is **$420.35**.
